::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_18 — OrgPath and the IGA Market
:::


::: {.callout-note}
The Identity Governance and Administration market is mature, and it is converging. SailPoint, Saviynt, CyberArk, One Identity, Oracle, IBM, and Microsoft Entra increasingly offer the same primary surface — access requests, certifications, joiner/mover/leaver lifecycle, role and entitlement modeling, and segregation of duties, now with AI recommendations and non-human identity coverage on top. OrgPath is not a like-for-like entry in that market. It is a deterministic organizational-addressing substrate that an IGA platform's workflows compose against, and the part of the surface it owns is the part none of those platforms targets as a primary function — and that Microsoft's own dynamic groups, Administrative Units, Conditional Access, and PIM cannot be composed into either. This book tells the positioning and the journey; the normative contracts are [ADR-078](/docs/adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.html) (the fifteen-facet substrate), [ADR-035](/docs/adr/adr-035-orgpath-codebook-binding.html) (the codebook binding), and [ADR-040](/docs/adr/adr-040-drift-engine.html) (the drift engine), with the customer-facing specs in the [reference architecture](/customer-documents/reference-architecture/index.html).
:::
